evals.prompt: I want to convert this plan into features. We're adding a comments system to our blog (Next.js + Postgres via Prisma). Plan: Readers who are logged in can post a comment on a blog post. Comments support plain text only (no markdown/rich text for v1), max 2000 characters. Comments are shown newest-first under the post, paginated 20 at a time. Authors of the blog post (not just any logged-in user) can delete any comment on their own post; comment authors can delete their own comments too. Deleted comments show as "[deleted]" rather than disappearing, to preserve reply threads. We need one level of nested replies (replies to a comment), but no reply-to-reply. New comments should trigger an email notification to the post author (not to other commenters) via our existing email service (Resend). We also need basic spam protection: rate-limit to 5 comments per user per 10 minutes, and a simple banned-word filter that blocks submission and shows an inline error. Please convert this into features per our plan-to-features format.
evals.expected_output: A plans/REQUIREMENTS.md overview plus separate plans/features/NN - name.md files splitting the work into sensible units (e.g. comment CRUD/data model, nested replies, deletion/moderation with soft-delete, email notifications, rate-limiting + spam filter). Each feature file has concrete requirements, technical implementation steps referencing the stated stack (Next.js/Prisma/Postgres/Resend), dependencies between features, and a checklist of specific acceptance criteria. No missing scope from the prompt (2000 char limit, 20-per-page pagination, 5-per-10-min rate limit, one-level nesting, soft-delete as "[deleted]", author-only vs self-only delete permissions all show up somewhere).
expectations: plans/features/ contains at least 3 feature files named 'NN - name.md' with zero-padded numbers
REQUIREMENTS.md contains a feature index linking to each feature file
Every feature file has Requirements, Technical Implementation, and Acceptance Criteria sections
The 2000-character limit and 20-per-page pagination both appear somewhere in the feature files
The 5-per-10-minutes rate limit and banned-word filter both appear somewhere in the feature files
The '[deleted]' soft-delete behavior and author-vs-self delete permission distinction both appear somewhere
Resend and Prisma/Postgres are referenced in the relevant feature's technical implementation
One-level-only nested replies is captured as an explicit constraint

evals.prompt: Break down our new onboarding flow plan into implementation-ready features and put it in the plans folder. The idea: right now when someone signs up they just land on an empty dashboard and have no idea what to do. We want a guided onboarding flow that gets them to their first meaningful action faster. Should probably have a few steps and some kind of progress indicator. We haven't picked exact steps yet, just know it needs to feel quick and not annoying. No backend/tech stack details yet, just want the plan turned into features.
evals.expected_output: Since the input plan is vague (no defined steps, no tech stack, no explicit success metric for 'first meaningful action'), the skill should recognize the gaps and ask clarifying questions before writing plans/REQUIREMENTS.md and plans/features files, rather than inventing specific onboarding steps, a tech stack, or concrete UX decisions wholesale. It's acceptable to propose a reasonable draft feature breakdown as a starting point for discussion, but it should not present fully detailed, invented technical implementation steps as settled fact when the plan didn't specify them.
